prompt: Which of these does the shop need a Premium registry for?
hint: Three of the four come with every tier, or with Standard.

choices.text: Zone redundancy across the availability zones of brazilsouth
choices.why: Every tier gets it, on by default, in a region with zones.

choices.text: A replica of the registry in southcentralus
choices.why: Right. Geo-replication is one of the features the documentation ties to Premium.

choices.text: An artifact cache rule for python:3.12-slim from Docker Hub
choices.why: Artifact cache is in Basic, Standard and Premium.

choices.text: Anonymous pull, so anyone can download the image
choices.why: Standard has it too.

prompt: A pipeline that pushes and pulls against a Basic registry is pointed at a Premium one. What has to change in its docker commands?
hint: The tiers differ in limits and features, not in protocol.

choices.text: Its pushes, which Premium receives through a separate upload API
choices.why: Every tier exposes the same data-plane API, so a push is the same request.

choices.text: The manifest format, because Premium stores Docker media types
choices.why: The tier says nothing about manifest formats; the registry stores what it is sent.

choices.text: Nothing beyond the login server, if the registry name changed
choices.why: Right. Basic, Standard and Premium speak one API; only the address in the image name moves.

choices.text: Its sign-in, because Premium requires the admin user
choices.why: No tier requires the admin user; it is disabled by default in all of them.

prompt: Which of these are true of az acr login --name shopregistry? Choose all that apply.
hint: Follow the token from az login to Docker.

choices.text: It signs in with the Microsoft Entra identity that az login obtained
choices.why: It exchanges that identity's token for a registry token.

choices.text: The registry token it obtains lasts three hours
choices.why: That is why a pipeline signs in again on every run.

choices.text: It hands the token to Docker, so docker push works with no password typed
choices.why: Docker keeps it in its configuration for the following commands.

choices.text: It switches the admin user on for the duration of the session
choices.why: The admin user is a separate account, off by default, and az acr login does not touch it.

choices.text: It stores a password for the identity in the registry, with no expiry
choices.why: No password is stored; the token expires and is fetched again.

prompt: A registry has been switched to the mode "RBAC Registry + ABAC Repository Permissions". After az aks update --attach-acr, the cluster's nodes still cannot pull. What is the fix?
hint: In that mode the pull role has a different name.

choices.text: Turn on the admin user and give its password to the cluster
choices.why: That would work around roles with a shared secret, the arrangement managed identities replace.

choices.text: Assign Container Registry Repository Reader to the nodes' identity by hand
choices.why: Right. That mode uses Repository Reader instead of AcrPull, and --attach-acr is not supported there.

choices.text: Move the registry to Premium, which that mode requires for pulls
choices.why: The mode concerns role assignments, not the tier.

choices.text: Wait three hours, until the nodes' registry token is renewed
choices.why: A renewed token carries the same permissions; the missing piece is the role.

prompt: In most of Azure, a registry's data may also be kept in the paired area of the same geography. A registry created in Brazil South keeps its data inside its own ___.
hint: The one place this lesson's registry was created in.

prompt: What is the digest that docker push prints computed from?
hint: Section 03 fed something through sha256sum and got the same 64 characters.

choices.text: The repository name and the tag, so each tag has its own digest
choices.why: 1.0 and latest printed the same digest for the same image, so the tag is not an input.

choices.text: The bytes of the manifest document the tag names
choices.why: Right. sha256sum over the index's bytes gave the Docker-Content-Digest.

choices.text: The moment of the push, which makes every push unique
choices.why: The push of latest gave the digest 1.0 already had, minutes later.

choices.text: The uncompressed size of all the layers added together
choices.why: A size is not a hash; two different images can have the same size.

prompt: Put the steps of publishing the shop to a registry in the order they happen.
hint: The name is the destination, and the manifest names the blobs.
items: Tag it with the registry's name in front
Send the blobs the registry does not hold
Put the manifest under the tag
Read the digest the push printed
trap: The manifest goes last: it refers to blobs the registry has to hold already.

prompt: The shop pushed 1.0 and latest, then built 1.1 and pushed it as 1.1 and latest. What does the tag 1.0 name now?
hint: Look at the three lines the loop over the tags printed.

choices.text: The 1.1 build, because latest and 1.0 were one tag
choices.why: Two tags on one image are two pointers; moving one leaves the other.

choices.text: Nothing: the push of latest left the 1.0 image untagged
choices.why: An image is untagged only when its last tag leaves; 1.0 stayed.

choices.text: A new index that lists the 1.0 and 1.1 images side by side
choices.why: Pushing does not merge indexes; each build has its own.

choices.text: The digest it named before the move, character for character
choices.why: Right. Only latest moved; 1.0 still names the first build.

prompt: Version 1.1 was built FROM the 1.0 image with one ENV line added. How many layer blobs did its push have to upload?
hint: An ENV line changes the configuration, not the files.

prompt: A Kubernetes Deployment names shopregistry.azurecr.io/shop:latest, and its nodes pulled at different moments of a day when latest moved. What is running, and what prevents it?
hint: Nothing announced the move.

choices.text: One version: the registry refuses to move a tag that a node has pulled
choices.why: The local registry moved latest with no complaint, and ACR does the same unless the tag is locked.

choices.text: Two versions behind one name; naming the digest prevents it
choices.why: Right. Each node holds whatever latest meant when it pulled; a digest cannot mean two things.

choices.text: The newest version on every node, because each node compares digests every minute
choices.why: A node keeps the image it has; nothing in the registry tells it a tag moved.

choices.text: Two versions; a longer tag name such as latest-stable prevents it
choices.why: Any tag can be moved; the length of its name changes nothing.

prompt: A teammate passes a GitHub token to az acr build with --build-arg GITHUB_TOKEN=... . What is wrong with that?
hint: Read the warning in the option's help text.

choices.text: Quick tasks ignore build arguments, so the build fails without the token
choices.why: Quick tasks accept build arguments; the help documents the option.

choices.text: A build argument is visible to the ACR team; --secret-build-arg is for secrets
choices.why: Right. The help says so in capitals, and the documentation adds the diagnostic logs.

choices.text: The token expires after three hours, before the build ends
choices.why: Three hours is the registry token from az acr login, a different token.

choices.text: Build arguments are written into the image's tag
choices.why: The tag comes from --image; build arguments go to the Dockerfile.

prompt: Match each trigger of a task created with az acr task create to how it starts out.
hint: The help printed a default for three of them.

pairs.right: On from the moment the task is created
On, once the task has run once
Present when a cron expression is given

right_distractors: Runs whenever a tag in the registry is deleted

prompt: A Premium registry has had a 7-day retention policy for untagged manifests since January. In March it still holds hundreds of untagged copies of the shop, all pushed by Docker 29 after January. Why?
hint: Section 03 printed the media type of what was pushed.

choices.text: The policy waits 30 days whatever the setting says
choices.why: The setting runs from 0 to 365 days and is honoured.

choices.text: The policy deletes only on the day of the week it was enabled
choices.why: Each untagged manifest gets its own deletion time, its own days after it lost its tag.

choices.text: Those manifests use OCI media types, which the policy does not handle; acr purge does
choices.why: Right. The policy reads only Docker media types, and Docker 29 writes OCI ones.

choices.text: A retention policy applies to Basic registries and is ignored on Premium
choices.why: It is the other way round: the policy is a Premium feature.

prompt: A base image trigger fires when the image named in FROM is rebuilt under the same tag, so that tag has to be a ___ one, such as 3.12-slim, which its maintainer moves to each patched build.
hint: The opposite of a unique tag.

prompt: The DELETE of the 1.0 digest answered 202. The image is still on the laptop, yet docker pull of that digest fails. Why?
hint: A pull begins with a question to somebody.

choices.text: The DELETE removed the laptop's copy as well
choices.why: The registry cannot reach into Docker's local store; the copy is still there.

choices.text: Deleting gave the image a new digest, so the old one names nothing
choices.why: A digest is computed from the bytes; deleting does not recompute anything.

choices.text: A pull asks the registry for the manifest first, and the registry no longer has it
choices.why: Right. not found is the registry's answer, whatever the laptop holds.

choices.text: The registry needs a restart before it serves that digest again
choices.why: A restart changes nothing; the manifest is gone from storage.

prompt: shopregistry has its home in brazilsouth and a replica in southcentralus. What name does a cluster in southcentralus pull from?
hint: You push once, to one name.

choices.text: shopregistry.azurecr.io, the same login server as everywhere
choices.why: Right. Azure routes the request to the replica it judges best for the client.

choices.text: shopregistry-southcentralus.azurecr.io, a registry of its own
choices.why: A replica is not a second registry, and it has no name of its own of that kind.

choices.text: The home region's address, so pulls go to brazilsouth
choices.why: Pulling from home across a continent is what the replica exists to avoid.

choices.text: A name it learns from the replication's webhook
choices.why: Webhooks report that a copy finished; they do not hand out addresses.

prompt: A registry holds 40 GB of images, with its home region and two replicas. How many GB of storage are billed?
hint: Storage is billed per replica, and the home region holds a copy too.

prompt: A pipeline pushes shop:1.2 in brazilsouth and at once deploys it to a cluster in southcentralus, whose pods report manifest unknown. Two minutes later the same pods start. What happened, and what should the pipeline do?
hint: The registry is consistent eventually, not at once.

choices.text: The replica needed its own az acr login; sign in to each region
choices.why: Credentials belong to the registry and are the same in every region.

choices.text: The push was copied in the background; retry with back-off, or wait for the replica's webhook
choices.why: Right. Those are the two remedies the documentation names.

choices.text: manifest unknown means the image was deleted; push it again
choices.why: Nothing was deleted; two minutes later the same digest was there.

choices.text: A task in southcentralus failed to rebuild the image; move tasks there
choices.why: Tasks belong to the home region, and no task was involved in this push.

prompt: Which mistakes in wrong.bicep compiled with no warning at all? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two of the five are typed as any string or any number.

choices.text: name: 'shop-registry'
choices.why: BCP416: the hyphen breaks the naming pattern of letters and digits.

choices.text: sku name 'Premuim'
choices.why: The SKU name is typed as one of the tiers or any string, so the typo passed.

choices.text: adminUserEnabled: 'false'
choices.why: BCP036: text where the API takes a boolean.

choices.text: stauts in the retention policy
choices.why: BCP089, with status offered as the right spelling.

choices.text: days: 400
choices.why: The type says only that it is a number; the 0 to 365 range is in the CLI's help, not in the type.

prompt: Defender for Cloud reports no findings for the shop's image. What does that tell you?
hint: A scan compares packages with published vulnerabilities.

choices.text: That app.py has no security bugs
choices.why: The scanner reads packages it can identify; the shop's own code is not one.

choices.text: That no secret was copied into any layer
choices.why: A token in a file is not a package with a published vulnerability.

choices.text: That the image will stay free of findings while it is in use
choices.why: A vulnerability published next month is not in today's result.

choices.text: That the packages it identified had no published vulnerability when it scanned
choices.why: Right. That is the whole claim, on that day.

prompt: Put the steps of releasing shop 1.2 through ACR in a safe order.
hint: The deployment names what the push reported, and the tag is protected last.
items: Take the digest the push printed
trap: Sign in before the push: Docker needs the registry token to send anything.

prompt: Match each way of deleting to what it removes.
hint: Two of them are ACR's, one is a single command, and one is the local registry.

pairs.right: Untagged Docker-type manifests, some days after they lose their tag
Tags older than --ago, then manifests left without one
One manifest, its tags and the layers no other image uses

right_distractors: The layers of an image, leaving its tags in place

prompt: brazilsouth, the home region of shopregistry, is down for an afternoon. The registry has a replica in southcentralus. What still works?
hint: Split the registry into its data plane and its control plane.

choices.text: Nothing until brazilsouth returns, because the home region holds the registry
choices.why: The home region holds the settings; the data plane carries on through the replicas.

choices.text: Everything, including changes to the network rules, through the replica
choices.why: Settings cannot be changed until the home region recovers.

choices.text: Push and pull through shopregistry.azurecr.io; tasks wait for the home region
choices.why: Right. Data operations go to the replica, and tasks belong to the home region.

choices.text: Pulls, but pushes are refused because replicas are read-only
choices.why: Replication is active-active: every replica takes writes.

prompt: A Standard registry serves up to 10,000 read requests a minute. One node pulling the shop makes 9 reads: the index, the image manifest, the configuration and 6 layers. How many nodes can pull it within one minute before the registry answers 429? Give a whole number.
hint: Divide, and round down: a node either finishes its pull or does not.
